description: The Igniters is a team of young data analysts aspiring to find a solution for Flame in Firefall. We have analyzed the 24 PSI investigations to provide better understanding about how flames behave in microgravity.
summary: Flame in Freefall is a web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion research into fire-safety insight for crewed habitats. NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository holds 24 combustion investigations and 1,943 test rows, but they are spread across 22 differently formatted tables and are hard to find, compare and interpret. We cleaned all of it into common units and mapped every test onto the oxygen and pressure it was burned at. Users pick a habitat (ISS cabin, Moon base or rover, or spacesuit) and see which experiments matter most, ranked by a transparent rubric with a reason for every point. IgniterX, our AI librarian, answers questions using only NASA sources and cites every claim. The map also exposes what has never been tested: only 66 of 1,943 test rows match a planned Moon base atmosphere, none burned a solid material, and none ran in Moon gravity. That shows engineers what is known and shows NASA where to test next.
